evidence.claim: The official biography identifies Abdel Fattah El-Sisi as Egypt's eighth president and lists his prior command roles, including commander-in-chief and minister of defense.
evidence.title: President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi
evidence.publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The official biography identifies Abdel Fattah El-Sisi as Egypt's eighth president and lists his prior command roles, including commander-in-chief and minister of defense.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary state biography for the incumbent ruler; stable office-identity evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to El-Sisi's office and prior military authority; not a claim about nuclear conduct.
contrary_evidence: Biography is self-authored state material and does not by itself prove how he used authority in 2022.

evidence.claim: The constitution text makes the president head of state and executive power, sets a six-year term with no more than two consecutive terms, and gives the president treaty, cabinet, and armed-forces powers with legislative checks.
evidence.title: Constitution of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The constitution text makes the president head of state and executive power, sets a six-year term with no more than two consecutive terms, and gives the president treaty, cabinet, and armed-forces powers with legislative checks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Canonical constitutional text for formal authority and constraints in force in the post-amendment period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Office-level authority, not personal nuclear behavior.
contrary_evidence: Formal powers on paper do not prove the degree of practical discretion in Egypt's political system.

evidence.claim: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had spearheaded the state-led investment strategy Sisi pursued and controlled a vast economic portfolio, including public works, land access, and multiple civilian sectors.
evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.excerpt: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had spearheaded the state-led investment strategy Sisi pursued and controlled a vast economic portfolio, including public works, land access, and multiple civilian sectors.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Serious policy analysis with detailed sectoral description and explicit attribution to Sisi's state-led strategy, though it remains interpretive rather than official data.
evidence.period_fit: describes the inherited structure and active 2022 state-led model
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Sisi as the central executive sponsor of the state-led investment model, though the military and other agencies executed much of it.
contrary_evidence: The paper also notes some practical benefits from military-managed infrastructure and housing.
It is an analytical assessment, not an audited balance sheet.

evidence.claim: Carnegie said the IMF had recognized Egyptian military companies as part of the SOE landscape and that many benefited from an uneven playing field, calling for competitive neutrality and stronger anti-monopoly rules.
evidence.title: Throwing Down the Gauntlet: What the IMF Can Do About Egypt's Military Companies
evidence.excerpt: Carnegie said the IMF had recognized Egyptian military companies as part of the SOE landscape and that many benefited from an uneven playing field, calling for competitive neutrality and stronger anti-monopoly rules.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed policy paper drawing on World Bank and IMF material; the claim is well-supported but still an expert synthesis.
evidence.period_fit: within 2022 and directly about the policy environment Sisi faced
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-era political economy because it describes the state and military privileges operating under his presidency, though the paper itself is analytical.
contrary_evidence: The paper also notes the government had begun discussing private-sector empowerment and state-asset consolidation.
It does not itself prove that reforms were not attempted.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker governor of the central bank after Tarek Amer resigned during the currency crisis, and that Abdalla had senior banking experience and had supported liberal economic policies.
evidence.title: Egypt's Sisi names Hassan Abdalla as caretaker cbank head
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker governor of the central bank after Tarek Amer resigned during the currency crisis, and that Abdalla had senior banking experience and had supported liberal economic policies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a concrete appointment, with background on the appointee's credentials and policy orientation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as president making the appointment; competence inference is limited to Abdalla's background and market reaction.
contrary_evidence: The post was caretaker/acting, so it shows a personnel response more than a durable institutional choice.
The source does not show that Abdalla changed policy outcomes by itself.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rose to 18.7 percent in November 2022, the highest since 2017, after the October currency devaluation and continued import restrictions.
evidence.title: Egypt inflation jumps to five-year high of 18.7% in November
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rose to 18.7 percent in November 2022, the highest since 2017, after the October currency devaluation and continued import restrictions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report using CAPMAS data, with a clear causal chain to policy and supply constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partially attributable to Sisi because the inflation spike also reflected external shocks, import shortages, and market conditions, but the devaluation and import restrictions were policy choices of his government.
contrary_evidence: The report itself cites supply shortages and higher production costs, so not all inflation is ruler-caused.
This is an outcome indicator, not a direct policy statement.

evidence.claim: The IMF approved Egypt's arrangement and said the package would shift to a flexible exchange rate, reduce the state footprint, level the playing field, strengthen governance and transparency, and expand social spending.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Approves 46-month US$3 billion Extended Arrangement for Egypt
evidence.excerpt: The IMF approved Egypt's arrangement and said the package would shift to a flexible exchange rate, reduce the state footprint, level the playing field, strengthen governance and transparency, and expand social spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF approval statement describing the agreed policy package and the rationale for it.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sisi's government as the borrower-side authority, but conditioned by IMF approval and implementation by the CBE, cabinet, and state agencies.
contrary_evidence: It is a program approval, not proof of implementation success by year-end.
It reflects external conditionality as well as domestic initiative.

evidence.claim: The World Bank announced new financing to expand Takaful and Karama, which as of June 2022 covered 3.69 million households; women were 74 percent of beneficiaries and 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank announced new financing to expand Takaful and Karama, which as of June 2022 covered 3.69 million households; women were 74 percent of beneficiaries and 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with direct program coverage and distribution details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government's social-protection apparatus, though the program was co-financed and shaped with the World Bank.
contrary_evidence: This shows mitigation and targeting, not a full answer to broad inequality or labor-market weakness.
It does not prove that the poor were adequately protected from inflation.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt lifted a key import restriction and that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi approved a list of 62 economic activities the state would leave to the private sector to meet IMF conditions.
evidence.title: Egypt lifts import curbs, backs bigger private sector role to meet IMF demands
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Egypt lifted a key import restriction and that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi approved a list of 62 economic activities the state would leave to the private sector to meet IMF conditions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a concrete policy move and a presidential approval tied to IMF conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as the president approving the list and to his government implementing the import-policy reversal; IMF conditionality and the dollar shortage were major external constraints.
contrary_evidence: The move was reactive and tied to IMF demands rather than an autonomous reform agenda.
The article notes continuing foreign-currency shortages and earlier devaluations.

unresolved_gaps: There is no direct 2022 ruler-attributed nuclear command, safety, or crisis decision in the file.
El Dabaa evidence is mostly permits, construction milestones, and project self-reporting, not independent safety enforcement.
The package shows mediation and diplomatic statements, but not the internal decision chain or independent proof that Egypt's mediation changed outcomes.
There is little direct evidence on any offensive military option or coercive-force decision in 2022.
The chain from abuse to personal or cabinet-level accountability is thin, especially for prisons, police, and protest repression.
The limited remedial evidence is not outcome-verified; pardons and release gestures need follow-through data.
There was no live national election in 2022, so contestability and succession are inferred largely from retrospective rights reporting.
The internal effect of dialogue initiatives and jail releases on pluralism is not independently shown.
Hard verification of State Ownership Policy implementation and actual divestments by year-end is thin.
Household-level welfare effects of inflation, transfers, and bread security are incompletely tied to ruler action.
The package lacks direct ruler-level attribution for social-welfare decisions beyond ministerial and partner-mediated actions.
There is little completed-outcome evidence for 2022 on poverty, learning loss, malnutrition, and sanitation after the interventions.
Direct evidence of personal assets, beneficial ownership, procurement gains, or family enrichment is still missing.
The file has one clear public denial and several propaganda or censorship claims, but fewer independently verified false statements with explicit contradiction.
The core 2022 economic program is reconstructed from speeches, policy papers, and partial implementation steps rather than a single explicit governing program document.
Independent verification of divestment, budget execution, and durable follow-through is still thin.
